hints: Look at line 5 of dispatch.sh. It builds a string out of $action and $target, then re-parses that whole string as shell source. Anything that ends up UNQUOTED in the built string becomes real shell syntax.

The target slot is wrapped in escaped quotes in the source, so a ; inside target alone doesn't break out — but action is not quoted at all. A semicolon (or any shell metacharacter) inside action ends the first command and starts a new one, which then runs for real.

Write answers.txt with line=5, flaw=eval-injection, and fix=... naming a case (or array) allowlist that dispatches directly instead of building and re-parsing a string. Then author hardened.sh from scratch: read $1/$2, match $1 against a small set of known verbs with a case statement, invoke the matching command directly on $target (never rebuild a string), and exit 2 for anything else. Test it with a real verb (must still work) and an injection-shaped action like 'x; rm -rf ~' (must be refused before anything runs), then lab check bash L3.7.
